newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African chemicals, oil strike not yet on cards.
newsitem.headline: S.African chemicals, oil strike not yet on cards.

text.p: Deadlocked talks between workers and employees in South Africa's strategic chemicals industry, including the oil sector, would go for conciliation later this month before any decision was taken on a possible strike.
"There is no strike on the cards now," Chemical Workers Industrial Union (CWIU) media spokesman Siphiwe Mgcina told Reuters on Monday.
He was commenting on reports that the union's national executive committee would decide on strike action at a meeting on Monday.
CWIU on June 26 applied to the Council for Conciliation, Mediation and Arbitration (CCMA) to intervene in its deadlocked dispute with employers over wages, working hours and maternity leave.
Mgcina said that the conciliation had been tentatively set for July 21 "and we will then see what our options are".

The industry has offered a 9.5 percent wage increase while the union is demanding 14.5 percent as well as a working week of 40 hours compared to the current average of 42. The union also wants six months maternity leave, four of which are fully paid.
